 1                                  SUMMARY OF ALLEGATIONS

 2          1.       This case concerns the collection, use, and disclosure of consumers’ videos, audio,

 3 and other private data by one of the largest advertising companies in the world.

 4          2.       This conduct starts with Meta “smart” glasses (hereinafter, “Meta Smart Glasses”),

 5 which Meta develops and sells through a partnership with Luxottica. The Meta Smart Glasses look

 6 like typical sunglasses or reading glasses, but have cameras built-in so that consumers can capture

 7 video, audio, and other content without needing to use a traditional camera or a smartphone.

 8 Consumers can enable the recording feature by saying the “wake-word” (“Hey Meta”) or by
 9 pressing a button on the glasses themselves.

10          3.       At no point did Meta or Luxottica disclose that these glasses served an entirely
11 different purpose: to capture private video, audio, and other content for profit, including to train

12 artificial intelligence (AI) models. To the contrary, they promised the exact opposite, repeatedly

13 touting that the Meta Smart Glasses were designed with “privacy” in mind and that consumers could

14 at all times control what videos, audio, or data were shared through the Meta Smart Glasses and

15 ultimately used by Meta.

16          4.       Each of these promises was a lie. Meta used consumers’ audio and visual recordings
17 captured through the Meta Smart Glasses to train its AI models, including videos and audio that

18 were captured when consumers did not say the wake-word or otherwise enable the video and audio

19 recording function. Consumers were never told Meta would use their private data for this purpose,

20 and certainly not when they themselves did not trigger this functionality.

21          5.       This conduct is particularly problematic because, once data enters Meta’s systems,

22 there are no controls over how this data is used or where it goes, nor is there any way to truly delete

23 it. Thus, consumers can never ensure their data is no longer used and have lost all control over this

24 private information.

25          6.       And, worse, Meta not only stored and used this audio and video content, but it

26 contractually agreed with a third party—Sama—to have independent contractors stationed in Kenya

27 manually review and annotate these videos specifically to improve its AI capabilities. These

17 conversations.
